title: Mobile, Baldwin County law enforcement trains to keep schools safe - NewsBreak
text: BALDWIN COUNTY, Ala ( WKRG ) — With the first day of school right around the corner, school resource officers from Baldwin and Mobile Counties spent the week in specialized training designed to keep students safe and prepare for emergencies. “These guys this week, they learned a lot about mental health, mental health awareness. Today, they’re learning how to do medical, tactical, medical response, medical response to some type of school shooting or violence incident right there, but they learned a lot of other stuff too,” Baldwin County Sheriff Anthony Lowery said. The program focuses on everything from first aid to trauma care and active shooter responses. Deputies say it’s not just about safety, though; it’s about building connections in the community. “Their first priority is to protect the school and the children, and their secondary mission is to build those relationships and help guide their path forward,” Mobile County Sheriff Paul Burch said. These officers have been able to make a serious impact in a number of different schools. “This was a game-changer for our school system. You know, you want your children to feel safe, you want parents to know that they’re sending their children off to a safe environment,” Baldwin County Superintendent Eddie Tyler said. Sheriff Lowery says that there’s one main reason why all this training is so important. “Because if you think about it, they’re protecting the number one resource in the state of Alabama, if not the country, and that’s our kids. If we can’t protect them and get them to grow, then we’re in trouble, not just as a state, but as a country,” said Lowery. For the latest news, weather, sports, and streaming video, head to WKRG News 5.
